title: Essential Services Are Now Missing Fuel
subtitle: Availability improved in Moscow and Saint Petersburg, but hospitals, firefighters and emergency vehicles still face supply failures elsewhere.

source.name: Tochnyi compilation of regional fuel availability reports

data.label: Vladimir region
data.detail: Five hospitals, including the region's main emergency unit, could not find sellers for their fuel tenders.

data.label: Krasnoyarsk
data.detail: Local fuel companies failed to supply firefighters; authorities opened a criminal case.

data.label: Tyumen
data.detail: Stations adopted a special timetable to refuel emergency vehicles, then availability deteriorated further.

data.label: Kursk region
data.detail: More than one third of filling stations have closed during the shortage.

data.label: Novosibirsk
data.detail: Russia's third-largest city remained in a severe and persistent shortage.

data.label: Mari El capital
data.detail: Volunteers remained at stations throughout the day to maintain order in fuel queues.

note: The pattern is uneven: major western cities improved while critical failures persisted in the south, east and regional public services.

metadata.keyFinding: Regional fuel failures have reached hospitals, firefighters and emergency vehicle operations.
